svg.title: Five lines, five silent ways to be wrong
svg.desc: The PyTorch training step drawn as five numbered stations - zero_grad, forward, loss, backward and step - with a big return arrow closing the loop and an amber annotation on each naming its characteristic silent failure, beside a separate evaluation block where model.eval and inference_mode are ticked and their wrong versions struck out, a crossed-out resume that loads the state dict without the optimizer, and bars comparing 41.2 against 27.8 milliseconds per step.
svg.text: Five lines, five silent ways to be wrong
the graph is BUILT here, fresh,
raw logits in. Adding a softmax
the graph is TRAVERSED and then
the only line in the loop that
the graph is rebuilt every single iteration.
That is exactly why you can put an if
the EVAL loop is a different loop
...and how do you know it resumed right? -> plot the metric across the kill
